about.text: The fat-rich part of raw milk, skimmed off as it rises or spun off in a separator, usually at 35–40 % fat. Pasteurised, standardised and soured, it becomes all the creams.

sources.text: An eighth by weight of the 193 Mt separated: the cream for about 8.5 Mt of butter and ghee made outside the home (of 13.2 Mt of butter and milk fat in 2023, half of it in India), at about 2 kg of cream a kilo, and about 5.5 Mt sold as cream.

how.text: The fat is lighter than the rest of the milk. Left to stand it floats up as a layer; in a dairy a centrifugal separator does the same in seconds and sends cream and skimmed milk out of separate outlets.

steps.note: Butterfat is lighter than milk, rises and is skimmed off the top before homogenisation; industrially centrifugal separators spin the cream out of the milk.
